text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementTechnologyOur Messy Cyborg Past and FutureMike Jay, author of “Wireheads,” on the murky borderlands where the science and fiction of mind control meetKFBy Kristen French9:00 AM CDT on October 14, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleA few decades ago, cultural historian and author Mike Jay stumbled onto the unfortunate story of James Tilly Matthews. In 1797, Matthews was locked in a London psychiatric hospital known colloquially as Bedlam because he had become convinced that his mind was being controlled by a machine he called the “air loom.” That machine, he believed, manipulated his mind via a magnet that had been secretly planted in his brain by political operatives.This was a florid fantasy, but Jay was fascinated by the echoes Matthews’ delusion contained of many real-life, cutting-edge technologies in development in the 1980s, two centuries later. As Jay attempted to trace the history of ideas about brain-technology hybrids back to their points of origin, he realized that such cyborgian notions had persisted throughout the industrial age.
